---
title: "5. Hysteresis (Double Saddle-Node)"
sidebar: usage
jupyter: python3
---

A small constant tilt added to the pitchfork unfolds it into a hysteresis
curve with **two** saddle-node bifurcations:

$$
\dot x = a + x - x^3.
$$

The bifurcation diagram in $(a, x)$ is the classic S-curve with two folds
($\dot{} = $ vertical tangents). Reproduces `Hysteresis.png`.

```{python}
from tvbo import Dynamics, Continuation, SimulationExperiment

HY_YAML = """
name: Hysteresis
description: Double saddle-node / hysteresis $\\dot x = a + x - x^3$.
parameters:
  a:
    name: a
    value: 0.0
state_variables:
  x:
    name: x
    domain: { lo: -2.0, hi: 2.0 }
    equation:
      lhs: Derivative(x, t)
      rhs: a + x - x**3
    initial_value: 1.0
"""

CONT_YAML = """
name: hy_in_a
dynamics: Hysteresis
free_parameters:
  - name: a
    domain: { lo: -2.0, hi: 2.0 }
max_steps: 600
ds: 0.005
bothside: true
"""

dyn = Dynamics.from_string(HY_YAML)
cont = Continuation.from_string(CONT_YAML)
exp = SimulationExperiment(dynamics=dyn, continuations=[cont])
```

## BifurcationKit.jl

```{python}
result_jl = exp.run("bifurcationkit.jl")
result_jl.continuations["hy_in_a"].plot(VOI="x")
```

## PyRates / PyCoBi

```{python}
result_py = exp.run("pyrates-bifurcation")
result_py.continuations["hy_in_a"].plot(VOI="x")
```

## AUTO-07p (NumCont)

Direct analogue of the standalone `DoubleSaddleNode.py` example. AUTO-07p
time-integrates from the model defaults to land on the upper stable branch,
then sweeps $a$ in both directions so both saddle-nodes are picked up in a
single merged diagram.

```{python}
result_auto = exp.run("auto-07p")
result_auto.continuations["hy_in_a"].plot(VOI="x")
```

The two saddle-node points at $a = \pm\,2/(3\sqrt 3) \approx \pm 0.385$ frame
the bistable region. Sweeping $a$ slowly from left to right and back traces
out the hysteresis loop characteristic of switching dynamics.
